# CSIT6000V (L1) - Advanced AI Computing and Systems Assignment 1: MPI Programming Submission deadline: October 22, 2026, 23:59

### II. Problem Description

This assignment focuses on the MPI parallelization of a General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) operator.

Given

 $$ A\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times K} $$ 

and

 $$ B\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times N}, $$ 

GEMM computes

 $$ C=A\times B,\qquad C\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times N}, $$ 

where

 $$ C_{i j}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}A_{i k}B_{k j}. $$ 

In the sequential version, GEMM is computed by a single process.

In this assignment, you will parallelize GEMM using a simple 1D row partitioning strategy.

Matrix A is divided by rows among MPI processes, while every MPI process uses the complete matrix B. Each process computes its assigned rows of C, and the local results are finally gathered to Process 0.

### III. Sequential Algorithm

Algorithm 1: GEMM (sequential)

Input:
matrix A of size $M \times K$
matrix B of size $K \times N$

1. Procedure GEMM(A, B, M, K, N):
2. initialize $C[M][N]$ to zero
3. for i from 0 to $M - 1$ do:
4. for j from 0 to $N - 1$ do:
5. $C_{ij} = 0$
6. for k from 0 to $K - 1$ do:
7. $C_{ij} = C_{ij} + A_{ik}B_{kj}$
8. end for
9. end for
10. end for
11. return C
12. end procedure

### IV. Your Implementation Task

The code skeleton "gemm_mpi.c" is provided.

Your task is to complete the missing code in the designated section of the main function.

1. Scatter the rows of matrix A to the MPI processes and make matrix B available to every MPI process.

2. Perform the local GEMM computation in each process:

 $$ l o c a l\_{C}=l o c a l\_{A}\times B. $$ 

3. Gather all local result blocks to Process 0 and assemble them into the complete output matrix C in the correct row order.

## Notes:

### 1. Row Partitioning

For all provided and evaluation test cases, the number of rows $M$ will be divisible by the number of MPI processes $P$:

 $$ M\bmod P=0. $$ 

Therefore, every MPI process receives the same number of rows of matrix A.

### 2. A typical implementation may use

## MPI_Bcast, MPI_Scatter, and MPI_Gather

Equivalent MPI communication methods that correctly implement the required parallel computation may also be used.

3. The sequential GEMM implementation is provided for reference and result comparison.

4. For more information about MPI APIs, refer to the MPI documentation introduced in the tutorial.

If a local MPI environment is not available, or if you want to verify your implementation in the official course environment, you may use the provided TACC SDK workflow.

This step is required only once on each computer.

Here,

### 6. Example MPI execution

Compile the MPI program:

mpicc gemm_mpi.c -02 -o gemm_mpi

Run with one MPI process:
mpiexec -n 1 ./gemm_mpi ./dataset/test1.txt
Run with two MPI processes:
mpiexec -n 2 ./gemm_mpi ./dataset/test1.txt

For every tested process count  $ P $, the test cases will satisfy

 $$ M\bmod P=0. $$

Programs will be evaluated using multiple matrix dimensions and valid MPI process counts.

Evaluation focuses on correctness and correct MPI-based parallel execution.

Performance and parallel speedup will not be evaluated.

### 3. Grading rubric

## • 10 points

The program successfully passes the required multi-process MPI executions and produces correct results for all evaluation test cases.

## • 5 points

The program produces correct results in single-process execution, but does not successfully pass the required multi-process MPI evaluation.

## • 0 points

The program fails to compile, fails to execute correctly, or produces incorrect results.

No performance or speedup measurement is included in the grading.
